name: Hydroxyzine
executiveSummary: First-generation sedating H1 antihistamine. Adult pruritus: **25 mg PO at night** up to **25 mg 3–4×/day**. Anxiety: **50–100 mg/day** divided. Pediatrics: **1–2 mg/kg/day** PO divided (max by age).
indications:
## Indications

- Pruritus (urticaria, dermatitis); mild–moderate anxiety; sedative premedication (PO/IM per label).

## Precautions

- QT prolongation — avoid with other QT+/hypokalemia; higher doses raise risk.
- Marked sedation; no driving; potentiates alcohol/opioids/benzodiazepines.
- Elderly: low doses; anticholinergic/fall risk.

> Prefer non-sedating antihistamines for daytime rhinitis alone.

adulto.dose: Pruritus: **25 mg PO at night**; if needed **25 mg q6–8h** (usual max **100 mg/day** for itch). Anxiety: **50–100 mg/day** in 2–3 doses (some labels up to **300 mg/day** — specialist only).
adulto.administration: PO; IM only with injectable hospital presentation.

pediatrico.dose: **1–2 mg/kg/day PO** divided q6–8h. Guide: >6 y often **12.5–25 mg** per dose; <6 y prefer mg/kg and syrup.
pediatrico.notes: Watch excess sedation and paradoxical excitation.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Somnolence, dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary retention, tachycardia; arrhythmia if QT prolonged.
